reason: The text demonstrates agency among non-leader groups. The ordinary Egyptian soldiers (וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם - 'the Egyptians pursued them') pursue the Israelites as active agents. Similarly, the Israelite people collectively (וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל - 'the Israelites went'; הָלְכ֥וּ - 'they walked') perform the action of traversing the sea as agents in their own right. While Moses and Pharaoh are formal leaders and God directs events, the text explicitly ascribes actions to non-leader populations who thereby demonstrate agency.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
